description:
MEASURED at fz-kdt.13.2 (release, `fz2 interp`, first-settlement timing off the public stream, three target fixtures).

Splitting analyze_activation into per-callsite / per-callee answers made mid-drive one-hop CLEANLINESS strictly finer (pinned by `compiler2_a_callee_ascent_leaves_the_callers_other_callsite_answers_clean`), and moved TRANSITIVE settledness by exactly zero:

  fixture               kind              settled-at-end before -> after
  enum_take_drop_split  ActivationInputs  222 -> 222
  enum_take_drop_split  Activation        131 -> 131
  range_map             CallSiteTargets    35 ->  35

(that is with the read-preservation rule off; with it on the counts fall, which is the removal of settledness that was resting on dropped subscriptions -- see fz-kdt.13.2's commit.)

Pre-drain first settlements are unchanged too: ActivationInputs 4-of-283 on enum_take_drop_split before AND after.

WHY: caller and callee read each other. `AnalyzeActivation(caller)` reads `ReturnType(callee)`; `AnalyzeActivation(callee)` reads `ActivationInputs(callee)`, which the caller publishes. Both publishers are clean long before either fact is transitively final, and no local counting rule can lower an `unfinal_reads` count inside a cycle -- only the drain arbiter can (`fact-engine.md`, *The drain arbiter*). Publisher identity is the wrong lever for that number; it was never the thing holding these facts unfinal.

CONSEQUENCE for fz-kdt.13 Story 4 (finality-first pop): its gate is 'the pop-time ready-alternative rate moved off 2%/0%/0%'. If the ready-alternative question is asked of TRANSITIVE finality it will still read ~0, for the reason above. Re-measure it against one-hop cleanliness (`unfinal_reads == 0` is the transitive question; `is_locally_settled` is the one the split actually improved) before building on it.

SECOND CAP, same measurement: a satisfied WAIT dirties EVERY answer a job holds, because a wait carries no derivation attribution (`Scheduler::enqueue_dependents`). Blocked completions are the main traffic (196 of 1,065 AnalyzeActivation evaluations on enum_take_drop_split), so a large share of re-dirtying is still job-wide by construction. Giving waits derivation attribution -- or splitting the job so a block scopes -- is the next real lever, and it is a separate design.
title: Analysis settledness is cycle-bound, so publisher granularity cannot move it
